The Arrival of Mijbil (7:52 - 12:46)
The Opening: Maxwell receives a sack from two Arabs containing his otter, Mijbil, with a note: "Here is your otter." (7:52 - 8:14)
The Bond: This event marked the beginning of a lifelong fascination/fixation with otters, a sentiment shared by most otter owners. (8:18 - 9:06)
Physical Appearance: Upon emerging, the creature resembled a small medieval dragon. Its fur was coated in mud, concealing a soft, chocolate-brown velvet coat beneath. (9:06 - 10:55)
The Cleaning Process: It took Maxwell nearly a month to remove all the mud and reveal the otter’s true, sleek color. (11:40 - 12:46)

2. Scientific Naming and Initial Behavior (12:46 - 13:45)
Scientific Classification: Mijbil belonged to a race previously unknown to science and was named Lutrogale perspicillata maxwelli (often referred to as Maxwell's otter). (12:46 - 13:12)
Adaptation: 
First 24 hours: The otter was indifferent and aloof, sleeping on the floor far from the bed. (13:16 - 13:28)
Second night: Mijbil became comfortable, joining Maxwell on his bed and sleeping in the crook of his knees. (13:28 - 13:38)

3. Characteristics and Playfulness (13:45 - 20:00)
Love for Water: Mijbil was obsessed with water, turning bathrooms into chaotic play zones, splashing, and rolling with joy—an essential otter trait. (14:09 - 14:49)
Intelligence: The otter was highly observant. Within two days, it learned to operate the bathroom faucet to get water, showing great ingenuity. (16:27 - 17:58)
Playful Nature: Mijbil played with rubber balls like a soccer player and would lie on his back to juggle marbles on his belly. (18:35 - 19:24)

Key Vocabulary
Indifferent: Having no particular interest or sympathy; unconcerned.
Aloof: Not friendly or forthcoming; cool and distant.
Fixation: An obsessive interest or attachment to someone or something.
Ingenuity: The quality of being clever, original, and inventive.
